formulations.strengths: UK product, per sachet: glucose 3.56 g, sodium chloride 0.47 g, potassium chloride 0.30 g, disodium hydrogen citrate 0.53 g; dissolve in 200 ml water

src.q: Glucose Sodium chloride Potassium chloride Disodium hydrogen citrate 3.56g 0.47g 0.30g 0.53g
Powder for reconstitution with 200ml water.

formulations.note: The clinic product lists trisodium citrate; the UK sachet uses disodium hydrogen citrate, so the exact electrolyte content may differ. Check the clinic product label for the amount of water per sachet.

formulations.label: Ready-to-drink oral solution
formulations.note: No UK SmPC was found for a ready-made oral rehydration solution. Content here comes from the UK sachet SmPC; the glucose and electrolyte content of a ready-made solution may differ, and the sachet reconstitution steps do not apply. Check the product label.

src.q: Glucose Sodium chloride Potassium chloride Disodium hydrogen citrate 3.56g 0.47g 0.30g 0.53g

items.t: Oral correction of fluid and electrolyte loss in infants, children and adults; watery diarrhoea of any cause, including gastroenteritis, in all age groups.

src.q: Oral correction of fluid and electrolyte loss in infants, children and adults.
Treatment of watery diarrhoea of various aetiologies including gastro-enteritis, in all age groups.

restrictions.note: No prescribing restrictions in the UK sachet SmPC (self-treatment limits are listed under cautions).

items.t: 1-2 sachets (each in 200 ml water) after every loose motion; more may be needed at first for full volume repletion.

src.q: Adults (including the elderly): One or two sachets after every loose motion.
More may be required initially to ensure early and full volume repletion.

items.t: Daily intake may be based on 20-40 ml/kg for adults and children (150 ml/kg for infants up to 2 years), adapted to age, weight, stage and severity.

src.q: Daily intake may be based on a volume of 150ml/kg body weight for infants up to the age of 2 and 20-40ml/kg body weight for adults and children.

items.t: Severe dehydration may first need parenteral fluids, then oral maintenance.

src.q: Severe dehydration may need to be corrected by parenteral fluids initially, followed by oral maintenance if indicated.

items.t: Infants under 2 years: use only under medical supervision and see a doctor as soon as possible; volume about 1 to 1.5 times the usual 24-hour feed volume (150 ml/kg/day).

src.q: Dioralyte shall not be used for treatment in infants below the age of 24 months without medical supervision.
Infants under the age of 2 years with diarrhoea should be seen by a physician as soon as possible.
Infants up to the age of 2: One to one and a half times the usual 24 hour feed volume.

items.t: Children: one sachet in 200 ml water after every loose motion.

src.q: Children: One sachet dissolved in 200ml of water after every loose motion.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or any excipient. No other known contraindications, but treatment may be inappropriate, e.g. intestinal obstruction needing surgery.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.
There are no known contraindications to Dioralyte.
intestinal obstruction requiring surgical intervention

items.t: Not for self-treatment (physician supervision needed) in chronic or persistent diarrhoea, liver or kidney disease, diabetes, low-potassium or low-sodium diets, or intestinal obstruction.

src.q: Dioralyte should not be used for self-treatment by patients: with chronic or persistent diarrhea. with liver or kidney disease. with diabetes. on low potassium or sodium diets. with an intestinal obstruction.
The use of Dioralyte in patients with these conditions should be supervised by a physician.

items.t: Reconstitute only with water, one sachet in 200 ml: a weaker solution is not optimal; a stronger one may cause electrolyte imbalance.

src.q: Dioralyte should not be reconstituted in diluents other than water.
a stronger solution than recommended may give rise to electrolyte imbalance

items.t: Diarrhoea lasting more than 24-48 hours: patient should see a doctor.

src.q: If diarrhoea persists for longer than 24-48 hours the patient should be seen by a physician.

items.t: Sodium: about 300 mg per sachet (15% of the WHO adult maximum daily intake of 2 g).

src.q: This medicinal product contains approximately 300 mg sodium per sachet, equivalent to 15% of the WHO recommended maximum daily intake of 2 g sodium for an adult.

interactions.note: The UK sachet SmPC section 4.5 says 'None stated'. The aluminium hydroxide/magnesium hydroxide SmPC states that aluminium hydroxide with citrates may raise aluminium levels (recorded under that medicine).

items.t: Kidney disease: not for self-treatment; use under physician supervision. After significant overdose, checking electrolytes is particularly important in severe renal failure.

src.q: Dioralyte should not be used for self-treatment by patients: with chronic or persistent diarrhea. with liver or kidney disease. with diabetes. on low potassium or sodium diets. with an intestinal obstruction.
The use of Dioralyte in patients with these conditions should be supervised by a physician.
This is particularly important in the very young and in cases of severe hepatic of renal failure.

items.t: With normal kidney function it is difficult to over-hydrate by mouth.

src.q: Where the kidneys are functioning normally, it is difficult to over-hydrate by mouth

items.t: Liver disease: not for self-treatment; use under physician supervision.

src.q: Dioralyte should not be used for self-treatment by patients: with chronic or persistent diarrhea. with liver or kidney disease. with diabetes. on low potassium or sodium diets. with an intestinal obstruction.
The use of Dioralyte in patients with these conditions should be supervised by a physician.

items.t: Not contraindicated in pregnancy; medical supervision is recommended.

src.q: Dioralyte is not contra-indicated in pregnancy or lactation.
Medical supervision is recommended for use during pregnancy and lactation.

items.t: Not contraindicated during breastfeeding; medical supervision is recommended.

src.q: Dioralyte is not contra-indicated in pregnancy or lactation.
Medical supervision is recommended for use during pregnancy and lactation.

items.t: For a breastfed infant with diarrhoea, breast milk need not be withheld.

src.q: However breast milk need not be withheld.

reproductive.note: No fertility or contraception statements in the UK sachet SmPC.

adverseCommon.note: The UK sachet SmPC section 4.8 says 'None stated'.

adverseSerious.note: The UK sachet SmPC lists no adverse effects ('None stated'); a too-strong solution may cause electrolyte imbalance (see cautions).

items.t: No improvement within 24-48 hours: the patient should be seen by a doctor.

src.q: If no improvement is seen within 24-48 hours it is recommended that the patient be seen by a physician.

items.t: Significant overdose: check serum electrolytes as soon as possible and monitor until normal.

src.q: In the event of significant overdose, serum electrolytes should be evaluated as soon as possible

items.t: Dissolve one sachet in 200 ml drinking water (freshly boiled and cooled for infants). Make up just before use; keep up to 24 hours in a fridge, otherwise discard after 1 hour. Do not boil the solution.

src.q: The contents of each sachet should be dissolved in 200ml (approx. 7fl oz) of drinking water.
For infants, and where drinking water is unavailable, the water should be freshly boiled and cooled.
may be stored for up 24 hours in a refrigerator, otherwise any solution remaining an hour after reconstitution should be discarded
The solution itself must not be boiled.

items.t: With vomiting, give small amounts frequently, but give the whole required volume.

src.q: When vomiting is present with the diarrhoea it is advisable that small amounts of Dioralyte be taken frequently.

items.t: At first stop all foods including cow's or formula milk (breast milk can continue); restart the normal diet gradually after 24-48 hours when symptoms settle.

src.q: In the initial stages of treatment of diarrhoea all foods, including cow's or artificial milk, should be stopped.
After 24 - 48 hours, when symptoms have subsided, the normal diet should be resumed but this should be gradual to avoid exacerbation of the condition.

items.t: If unsure of the amount, give more rather than less (when kidneys work normally).

src.q: where there is doubt about the dosage, more rather than less should be taken
